title.narrative: UNDP Effective, Inclusive and Accountable Institutions
UNDP Effective, Inclusive and Accountable Institutions

description.narrative:
Area 1 Anti-corruption: The purpose of the proposed programme is strengthening national capacities in selected countries in from Africa and Asia-Pacific regions to integrate anti-corruption in the SDGs. The main capacity development challenges that the intervention aims to address are: - Weak institutional capacity and political will to implement the anti-corruption targets of SDG 16; - Knowledge gaps in integrating anti-corruption in the SDGs; - Gaps in data and methodology to measure anti-corruption indicators; and - Coordination gaps between anti-corruption actors and SDG actors to monitor the 2030 agenda UNDP will address capacity development at three levels: individual (staff level, e.g knowledge and competencies); organisational level (e.g., mandates, functional capacity, resources, etc.); and macro/environmental level (e.g, overall coordination mechanisms, formal and informal structure, political economy environment, etc.) This is in line with Sidas view on capacity development. The different levels interact with and influence each other and the analysis should ideally include important relationships between these levels, rather than just list opportunities and challenges under each heading. How UNDP works with capacity development at different levels and how these levels interact, and how relevant actors are included in this process, is a dialogue question to follow-up.
Area 2 Legal Identity: This proposal aims to provide catalytic support to UNDPs legal identity efforts at both the country and global levels, via two priority work areas: • Seed funding support, either for project formulation, or the initial stages of project implementation, of One UN legal identity projects in the nine pilot countries. The focus of these projects can be along a range of potential support, including for example, digitizing the birth registration system, or drafting of a national identity strategy, or building the capacity of a new or existing civil registration authority mandated to roll out a national population register/national ID card scheme, etc. (Exact nature of interventions to be determined on a case by case basis following proper needs assessments). • Establish a sound methodology for accurately estimating the size of the population without legal identity and identify their key profile variables (e.g. women or language minorities, etc).

UNDP och Sida har haft en dialog under operationaliseringen av Sidas strategi för kapacitetsutveckling, partnerskap och metoder som stöder Agenda 2030 för hållbar utveckling rörande möjligheten att utforma ett strategiskt samarbete kring governance-frågor. UNDPs Chrisis Bureau and Bureau for Policy and Programme Support inkom så med ett förslag på områden som detta strategiska samarbete kunde omfatta. Efter dialog med UNDP har Sida och UNDP enats om att prioritera två områden i detta globala stöd: Strengthening National Capacities to Integrate Anti-Corruption in Sustainable Development Goals samt Legal Identity for All. Områdena har tydliga kopplingar till UNDPs långsiktiga strategiska plan samt relevans i förhållande till Sidas strategi, med bäring på såväl kapacitetsutveckling som samverkan och partnerskap. Sida föreslår därmed ett stöd om 26 000 000 SEK 2019-2022 till UNDP för institutionell, global kapacitetsutveckling med fokus på SDG16: fredliga och inkluderande samhällen. Insatsens två områden syftar till följande:
Strengthening National Capacities to Integrate Anti-Corruption in Sustainable Development Goals: Syftet med det föreslagna programmet är att stärka den nationella kapaciteten i utvalda länder i Afrika och Asien och Stillahavsområdet kring att integrera antikorruption i Sustainable Development Goals, SDGs. De viktigaste kapacitetsutmaningarna som insatsen ämnar adressera : - Svag institutionell kapacitet och politisk vilja att genomföra antikorruptionsmålen för SDG 16. - Kunskapsklyftor när det gäller att integrera antikorruption i SDGer; - Brister i data och metodik för att mäta indikatorer mot korruption, samt: - Koordineringsgap mellan aktörer mot korruption och SDG-aktörer i förhållande till Agenda 2030.
UNDP kommer att arbeta med kapacitetsutveckling på tre nivåer: individ,- organisatorisk,- och institutionell nivå. De olika nivåerna interagerar med och påverkar varandra och analysen bör därmed idealiskt innehålla viktiga förhållanden mellan dessa nivåer. Hur UNDP arbetar med kapacitetsutveckling på olika nivåer och hur dessa nivåer interagerar, och hur relevanta aktörer ingår i denna process, är en dialogfråga att följa särskilt följa upp, liksom risken för brist på politisk vilja.
Legal Identity for All: Syftet med detta förslag är att ge ett katalytiskt stöd till UNDP: s insatser inom Legal Identity på bilateral- och på global nivå via två prioriterade områden: • Stöd till projektformulering och inledande stadier av implementering av en "One-UN" - satsning inom Legal identity. Fokus kommer att ligga på en rad potentiellt stöd, inklusive till exempel digitalisering av födelseregistreringssystem, utarbetande av en nationell identitetsstrategi eller byggande av kapaciteten hos en ny eller befintlig civilregistreringsmyndighet som har mandat att hantera ett nationell befolkningsregister • Upprätta en metod för att uppskatta omfånget av personer som lever utan laglig identitet samt identifiera variabler ( ex minoriteter, barn, kvinnor etc) som är särskilt utsatta.

Anticorruption / ACPIS:
The ACPIS global project was launched in 2021 for a period of three-years in a tripartite partnership among Sida, Norad and UNDP. The ACPIS global team engaged Sida, Norad, UNODC, U4, UNDPs Independent Evaluation Office, and the UNDP Asia-Pacific and Africa regional hubs to select 11 countries [1] that benefited from policy and advisory support to integrate anti-corruption in SDGs. Of these countries, six (Bangladesh, DRC, Liberia, Rwanda, Tanzania, and Uganda) were fully or partially funded by Sida. These countries received capacity building support to implement innovative solutions aiming to promote transparency, integrity and accountability measures across various sectors.
By the end of December 2022, all six countries had established and deployed solid citizen-centric digital systems in environmental resource management, healthcare, justice, and public service delivery sectors. These systems proved to be instrumental in integrating anti-corruption solutions in national development plans and accelerating the achievement of the 2030 Agenda. Moreover, amidst the COVID-19 crisis, ACPIS strengthened the capacity of countries in integrating anti-corruption across various thematic areas by organizing a series of online capacity development events to reinforce results on the ground.
Those six country-level ACII projects partially or fully supported by Sida resources produced a total of 10 knowledge products in the form of studies, training materials, etc. (e.g., a baseline survey report on the Grievance Redress System in Bangladesh, Public Expenditure Tracking training package in Tanzania). These valuable resources were made possible due to the active engagement and contributions of 36 local activists and anti-corruption champions from those six countries. Moreover, the six target countries promoted anti-corruption reforms through development and revision of 13 laws and related legal documents. In addition, ACPIS provided policy and advisory support to countries by responding to their specific needs and demands. This support aimed to strengthen the capacities of key national actors to effectively integrate anti-corruption in SDGs and measure and monitor the progress of anti-corruption targets of SDG 16. In 2020-2022 (three years period) and working closely with major partners, around 60 countries across all regions, including 15 Sida priority countries, received support from UNDP global, regional and country level teams that resulted in the integration of anti-corruption measures into national plans and policies, as well as the establishment of robust anti-corruption mechanisms and systems that contributed to the implementation of the 2030 Agenda. This support was provided in drafting or revision of legal documents, development of national anti-corruption strategies, and knowledge brokering to implement anti-corruption strategies, among others.
[1] Bangladesh, DRC, Liberia, Malawi, Nepal, Nigeria, Rwanda, Sri Lanka, Tanzania, Uganda, and Vietnam.
In 2020-2022, as a facilitator and broker of anti-corruption knowledge, ACPIS promoted South-South and Triangular Cooperation on anti-corruption through global, regional and country-level events. In cooperation with a wide range of partners, including Sida, ACPIS organized or co-organized more than 40 events (e.g., webinars, online courses, training events policy dialogues, discussion forums, knowledge sharing workshops, etc.) and engaged approximately 4,500 national counterparts, practitioners, CSOs, academia, independent experts, and donor and development partners to enhance global cooperation, empower stakeholders to act against corruption and promote anti-corruption practices worldwide.
From 2020 to 2022, together with donor and programme partners and UNDP's regional teams, ACPIS co-organized a total of 22 high-level events at the margins of global anti-corruption fora, namely eight workshops at the 19th International Anti-corruption Conference (IACC); seven special events on the sidelines of the 9th Session of the Conference of States Parties (CoSP) to UNCAC; and seven events at the margins of the 20th IACC. The ACPIS global team actively engaged Sida in all these events to feature Sidas anti-corruption strategy, knowledge and experiences. Moreover, these events significantly contributed to enhancing knowledge of the integration of anti-corruption in SDGs by bringing practical experiences from Sida-funded UNDP projects.
From 2020 to 2022, to enhance stakeholders knowledge on the linkages between anti-corruption and the SDGs, strengthen the capacity of practitioners to measure and monitor SDG 16 implementation, integrate anti-corruption across thematic areas, ACPIS developed seven global knowledge products, in addition to the 10 knowledge products developed by Sida-funded country level projects. These include i) a guidance note on Integrating Transparency, Accountability and Anti-Corruption in Socio-Economic Impact Analyses, Needs Assessment and Response to the COVID-19 Pandemic, ii) a guidance note on Transparency, Accountability and Anti-Corruption Service Offer for COVID-19 Response and Recovery, iii) a publication on New Technologies for Sustainable Development: Perspectives from integrity, trust, and anti-corruption, iv) a publication on Corruption and Contemporary Forms of Slavery, v) an online course on Anti-corruption in the Context of the 2030 Agenda, vi) an online course on Transparent and Open Public Procurement for Sustainable Development and vii) Toolkit to integrate anti-corruption in SDGs.
Throughout the project implementation phase, ACPIS prioritized the integration of gender equality across all its anti-corruption activities. Recognizing the importance of womens empowerment, ACPIS actively sought opportunities to strengthen the role of women in all aspects of its work. ACPIS organized capacity-building events and discussion platforms that directly benefited 2,400 women. These initiatives aimed to enhance womens knowledge and anti-corruption skills, empowering them to actively contribute to anti-corruption efforts. By prioritizing gender equality and creating inclusive spaces for women's participation in all its activities, ACPIS demonstrated its commitment to promoting diversity and ensuring that women have equal opportunities to engage in the acceleration of the 2030 Agenda.
Throughout the three years of the partnership between Sida and UNDP, the ACPIS global team actively engaged Sidas capacity building and anti-corruption units in every aspect of the project implementation, including monitoring and quality control, and engaged Sida in capacity building and advocacy events, political and economic analysis of countries, selection of countries, and development of knowledge products and online courses. Overall, given the objectives of this initiative and the actual results presented below, the ACPIS global project has achieved all three outputs envisioned by the UNDP-Sida Joint Technical Assistance for Asia and Africa project.
(Sida priority countries: Armenia, Belarus, Colombia, Cambodia, Iraq, Kenya, Kosovo, Moldova, Myanmar, North Macedonia, Serbia, Somalia, Turkey, Ukraine, Yemen.)
Legal Identity Project:
While there were some delays in the implementation, particularly on the country level, the project achieved some critical milestones in global and country work:
1. Increased capacity of UNCTs and Member States through policy guidelines which were developed during the reporting period such as i) mapping on the usage of biometrics technologies across UN system and ii) study on Risks of Exclusion, Discrimination and other Human Rights Concerns Related to the Design and Implementation of Digital Legal Identity Systems, which will lead to a practical toolkit for UNCT in 2023.
2. Enhanced understanding on the potential of digitalization and its risk through a series of discussions with leading private sector and discussion which also led to increasing awareness from private sector around legal identity issues on the importance to design and implement legal identity system in human rights based approach.
3. Provision of a comprehensive one-stop shop support to the Member States on legal identity from policy, programming, procurement and ICT perspectives which successfully identified the challenges of the Member States and recommended the best solutions that are fit for purpose of the Member States.
4. Implementation of One UN approach which led to seamless support to Member States in 6 countries. The success of these 6 countries were replicated and expanded in other 7 countries which were financed on its own.
5. Reduced number of people without legal identity: Through UNCTs programming, the number of people without legal identity were reduced. Though the actual number is still being calculated, the significant number of people were registered in Kenya and Zambia. Due to a request from one of the countries where one of the planned activities had to be postponed in 2023, the no-cost extension was granted until the end of April 2023.
A final evaluation of the overall global programme Legal Identity for All was conducted in 2022 which highlights the success of one UN approach and efficient and seamless support provided to the Member States.
